sentenceSets.sentence: The transient advantage of the early lead was lost before the team had built the infrastructure to make it permanent.

answerChoices.reasoning: Temporary means lasting for a limited time; while the advantage was temporary, 'temporary' is broader, whereas 'transient' emphasizes a short duration and fleeting quality.
Fleeting means lasting for a very short time; nearly synonymous with transient, but 'fleeting' emphasizes the brief, rapid passing, while transient emphasizes passing in and out of existence.
Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time; very close to transient, but 'ephemeral' emphasizes briefness, whereas 'transient' emphasizes the passing nature.
Short-lived means not lasting long; the advantage was short-lived, but this emphasizes brevity of life, whereas 'transient' emphasizes passing through without establishing permanence.
Brief means short in duration; while the advantage was brief, this emphasizes duration, not the quality of passing in and out.
Quick means rapid or sudden; while the advantage disappeared quickly, 'quick' emphasizes speed, not the nature of being transient.
Sudden means happening unexpectedly; while the advantage was unexpected, this doesn't emphasize the temporary nature.
Passing means going by or coming to an end; while the advantage was passing, the sentence emphasizes it was never established as permanent.
Permanent means lasting indefinitely; the advantage was transient, opposite of permanent, and was lost before being made permanent.
Enduring means lasting a long time; the transient advantage did not endure, opposite of enduring.
Stable means firmly established and lasting; the transient advantage was unstable and temporary, the opposite of stable.

sentenceSets.sentence: The transient population of the city—tourists, business travelers, and seasonal workers—made it hard to build community bonds.

answerChoices.reasoning: Temporary means lasting for limited time; the population was temporary, but 'temporary' is general, whereas 'transient' emphasizes people passing through rather than settling.
Visiting means staying somewhere temporarily; while transient people visit, 'visiting' emphasizes the act of visiting, not the nature of being in passage.
Itinerant means traveling from place to place; nearly synonymous with transient, but 'itinerant' emphasizes movement, whereas transient emphasizes lack of permanence.
Mobile means able to move or be moved; transient people are mobile, but 'mobile' emphasizes the capacity to move, not the temporary nature.
Shifting means changing or moving; the population was shifting, but this emphasizes change rather than the passing nature of individuals.
Changeable means prone to change; the population was changeable, but this emphasizes variability, not transience of individuals.
Floating means without fixed attachment; the population was floating, but 'floating' emphasizes lack of attachment, not passing nature.
Migratory means moving seasonally; some of the transient population were migratory, but this is more specific than the general term.
Permanent means staying indefinitely; the transient population consisted of people not staying permanently, opposite of permanent.
Settled means established in a place; transient people did not settle, the opposite of settled.
Rooted means deeply established; transient people passing through were not rooted, the opposite of rooted.

sentenceSets.sentence: The transient nature of their friendship—sustained only through brief encounters at conferences—seemed to suit both of them perfectly.

answerChoices.reasoning: Temporary means lasting for limited time; the friendship was temporary, but 'temporary' is general, whereas 'transient' emphasizes existing primarily in passing moments.
Fleeting means lasting very briefly; the encounters were fleeting, but 'fleeting' emphasizes the brevity of moments, whereas 'transient' emphasizes the passing nature of the connection.
Intermittent means occurring at intervals; the friendship was intermittent with encounters at conferences, but 'intermittent' emphasizes periodic resumption, not the transient nature.
Sporadic means occurring irregularly; the friendship was sporadic with brief conference encounters, but 'sporadic' emphasizes irregularity rather than the passing quality.
Brief means short in duration; the encounters were brief, but this emphasizes duration, not the transient nature of the friendship.
Casual means informal or relaxed; their friendship was casual, but this emphasizes the tone, not its transient nature.
Superficial means lacking depth; a transient friendship might be superficial, but the sentence emphasizes how well the arrangement suited them, not its superficial quality.
Surface-level means not deep; while the friendship might be surface-level, the sentence emphasizes the transient arrangement itself, not depth.
Permanent means lasting indefinitely; the transient friendship was not permanent, opposite of permanent.
Constant means continuous or always present; the transient friendship was not constant, the opposite.
Enduring means lasting a long time; the transient friendship did not endure, the opposite.
